bull_bear.body: 1) The 'multiplier effect' loss: International executive cancellations dragged down associated domestic team travel, amplifying the FTA hit beyond direct foreign bookings. 2) Accounting nuance: INR 800cr Capex WIP is split across CWIP (INR 132cr), IPUC (INR 486cr), and Inventory (INR 269cr), obscuring the true scale of work-in-progress if looking only at the CWIP line item. 3) Hyderabad strategy: Taking a 'warm shell' on lease from sister concern Mindspace REIT significantly reduces upfront land risk and back-ends capex, improving ROCE profile.

- The positioning slide claims "Disciplined capital allocation, strong balance sheet" and "Industry-leading asset management practices" as part of the Asset Ownership Foundation.

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical shocks disrupting travel and energy markets — The MD&A records that FY 2025-26 was marked by escalating trade tensions and tariff actions followed by the West Asia war, with disruptions around critical trade routes such as the Strait of Hormuz elevating input costs and disrupting trade flows and travel routes. Management states that a prolonged escalation could further weigh on global growth, and notes that beginning CY 2026 saw short-term impact from the West Asia war.
- Aviation ecosystem disruption and passenger traffic volatility — Hotel demand is highly correlated with aviation. The MD&A notes that Operation Sindoor and intermittent disruptions within the aviation ecosystem led to short-term uncertainty in travel sentiment and temporary volatility in passenger movement across select routes, and that March 2026 witnessed significantly lower air passenger traffic during the heightened turmoil, with complete normalcy potentially taking longer.
- Discretionary spending sensitivity and moderating RevPAR growth — The global hospitality outlook, while cautiously positive, remains challenged by continuing geopolitical uncertainties, elevated inflation and tighter financial conditions potentially impacting discretionary spending; management notes that amid elevated geopolitical uncertainty RevPAR growth is likely to moderate as pressure on travel sentiment and pricing power tempers performance.
- Inflation, energy price volatility and tighter financial conditions — The MD&A notes that inflation is anticipated to rise in CY 2026 before resuming its decline, driven largely by energy price volatility and supply-side disruptions, and that the RBI identified energy price volatility, geopolitical developments and climate-related disruptions as key upside risks to the inflation outlook. Growth is expected to be impacted by persistent supply-side risks, elevated energy prices and tighter financial conditions.
- Uneven and still-normalising inbound tourism recovery — Asia-Pacific international arrivals reached only approximately 91% of pre-pandemic levels in CY 2025, and India's Foreign Tourist Arrivals at approximately 90.2 lakh in CY2025 moderated over the prior year, remaining below pre-pandemic peaks and sensitive to global developments such as the West Asia conflict from March 2026.
- Cost pressures, labour constraints and sustainability compliance needs — Management states that over the next 3-5 years, while the industry moves into a structurally driven growth phase, cost pressures, labour constraints and sustainability needs will keep the focus on operational efficiency and differentiated experiences - a structural margin risk for an owned-asset hospitality operator.
- Development and execution risk in a long-dated, approval-heavy pipeline — The Board's Report describes multiple projects at different stages of completion (Airoli, Varca, Delhi Terminal 3, Madhapur Hyderabad, Kerala, Udaipur, CIGNUS Powai Tower 2), with the Bambolim resort dependent on approvals attained only post closure of the acquisition. The MD&A separately notes that supply is constrained by high development costs, land scarcity and lengthy approvals - the same conditions that create execution and timeline risk for Chalet's own pipeline.
- Financing and leverage exposure across a capital-intensive build-out — The Board's Report records that the Company avails credit facilities for capital expenditure, working capital and repayment of high-cost debt, and that during the year it availed additional borrowings and repaid existing debt, alongside outstanding debentures and commercial paper - leaving performance exposed to interest rates and refinancing conditions in a period the MD&A describes as one of tighter global financial conditions.
- Concentration in a single hospitality-plus-real-estate business and limited geographic spread — Per the BRSR, turnover is split only two ways - Accommodation and Food Service (62%) and Real Estate (38%) - across 11 hotels and one office in 5 states, with no international operations and no exports. Earnings therefore depend on a narrow set of Indian metro micro-markets.
- Regulatory and structural approval dependency, including the pending amalgamation — The Board's Report notes the Scheme of Arrangement and Amalgamation of Sonmil and Dukes with the Company has been filed and approval of the Hon'ble NCLT is awaited, leaving the intended corporate simplification and operational synergy contingent on a third-party approval.

outlook.body:
- Own and develop institutional-quality hospitality assets in India's most important commercial and travel destinations, complemented by high-quality Grade A commercial real estate developments
- Transition from a pure ownership model to an owner-operator framework, with the launch of ATHIVA marking a structural move toward operational control that lets Chalet capture full operator margins and reduce third-party management fees
- Build an in-house, standardised and scalable hotel management platform to ensure consistent service quality and faster execution of future expansion
- Prioritise an integrated urban cluster (mixed-use) model over standalone developments, where Grade A CIGNUS office assets create a captive corporate base driving weekday hotel occupancy and high-margin MICE demand
- Focus on strategic locations: 'big boxes' in key cities and commercial hubs for business hotels, and destinations within comfortable drivable distance of key airports for leisure
- Apply stringent return criteria (RoCE, payback) to every prospective investment, screening out smaller assets and remote locations to preserve management bandwidth and margins
- Asset sweating: maximise use of internal and external real estate within hotels, add F&B outlets through remodelling, and monetise surplus FSI at hotel locations
- Strategic diversification across geography and format, moving beyond Mumbai business hotels into leisure resorts and multiple metros
- Extend the ATHIVA brand across the existing portfolio and pipeline, creating a distinct growth vertical of destination resorts and standalone branded assets
- Increasingly evaluate brownfield opportunities, mixed-use developments and alternative structures to optimise capital efficiency amid rising development costs
- Invest in digital capabilities and technology to improve operational efficiency and personalise guest experiences
- Embed sustainability as business strategy: transition to a low-carbon economy, scale renewable energy, improve energy efficiency, reduce water consumption and strengthen waste management
- Strengthen the project management team to drive the several new projects in progress and deliver premium Grade A hospitality assets on time and within budget
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Chalet is pursuing a high-conviction growth strategy of disciplined acquisitions of large-format hospitality assets and greenfield development of luxury and upper-upscale hotels in high-demand, under-penetrated micro-markets, with a stated plan to expand hotel inventory by around 50% (approximately 1,655 keys) and leasable area by over 37% from 2.4 msf to 3.3 msf in the next few years, taking total portfolio including pipeline past the 5,000-key milestone. Under construction are CIGNUS Powai Tower II (0.9 msf, Mumbai, completion expected Q4 FY27), the Taj at Delhi International Airport Terminal 3 (380 rooms, with 70 rooms targeted for commissioning by Q4 FY27 and the balance in the subsequent quarter; described elsewhere in the report as an approximately 385-390 room hotel being developed by subsidiary Chalet Airport Hotel Private Limited under a franchise agreement with The Indian Hotels Company Limited), Athiva Resort & Spa at Varca, South Goa (205 rooms, awaiting local approvals, expected completion FY 2027-28), the Ritz Carlton at Madhapur Mindspace, Hyderabad (330 rooms, to be received on warm shell basis from an SPV of Mindspace Business Parks REIT by Q4 FY28 with launch targeted Q4 FY29) and the Hyatt Regency at Airoli, Navi Mumbai (276 rooms, environmental clearance received and excavation started, launch targeted Q4 FY29) - together approximately 1,190 rooms and 0.9 msf. In planning are a premium resort at Udaipur (approximately 144 rooms, under design and approval, expansion potential being evaluated), Athiva Resort & Spa at Bambolim, North Goa (approximately 170 rooms, timelines estimated at around 36 months post approvals which follow closure of the acquisition) and Athiva Resort & Convention Centre at Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala (approximately 150 rooms) - approximately 464 rooms in total. During FY 2025-26 the Company added 129 additional rooms at Bengaluru Marriott Hotel Whitefield (8 suites added during the year, taking the total to 520 keys including 121 keys added in FY 2024-25), expanded the Khandala resort from 80 keys to 147 keys through the addition of 67 new rooms and a complete makeover, relaunching it as Athiva Resort & Spa, Khandala, and upgraded and rebranded the Faridabad resort as Aravali Marriott Resort & Spa, NCR with a pool bar, club house and refresh of rooms and public areas. The 152-key Four Points by Sheraton at Vashi is under renovation and is proposed to be rebranded under the Athiva brand. Three corporate development initiatives were signed during the year: a Binding Term Sheet to acquire Lakeview Mercantile Company Private Limited (potential approximately 170 room luxury resort at Bambolim, Goa; due diligence stage, closing expected during FY 2026-27), a Memorandum of Understanding for a warm-shell lease of a building at Madhapur, Hyderabad for a proposed approximately 330 room luxury hotel with approximately 36,255 sq ft of commercial/retail space, and a Binding Term Sheet to acquire Seasons Hotels Private Limited, which owns a resort at Udaipur, Rajasthan with around 150 rooms - completed in May 2026 after the year end, marking Chalet's entry into Rajasthan. In the rental and annuity space, nine towers of the Koramangala, Bengaluru residential project have been completed and handed over, with Phase 2 (two towers, 168 apartments) and a commercial building of approximately 160,000 sq ft under construction and expected to complete in FY 2026-27; Phase II of the Koramangala commercial development (0.2 msf) is under construction as part of the expansion of annuity office assets. Total keys of the Company and its subsidiaries stood at 3,389 as on March 31, 2026 across 11 hotels, with 2.4 msf of Grade A commercial real estate operational at 88% occupancy including area committed, plus 0.9 msf under development in Mumbai and 0.16 msf in Bengaluru. Management notes that in light of increasing complexities and high development costs it will increasingly evaluate brownfield opportunities, mixed-use developments and alternative structures to optimise capital efficiency.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- ICRA expects Indian chain hotel demand to grow at a CAGR of 10.5% against supply CAGR of 9.1%, implying a sustained demand-supply gap
- Demand is underpinned by a broad mix of segments - business travel, leisure, MICE, weddings, pilgrimages and government/corporate delegations - supported by a growing economy, expanding travel infrastructure, new convention centres and wider airline connectivity
- Structural demographic shifts: urbanisation has risen from 28% (CY01) to an estimated 37% (CY24), still well below the US (84%), UK (85%) and China (67%); the middle class is projected to grow from 31% of population (FY21) to 61% by FY47
- Domestic tourism remains the dominant growth engine, with visitors projected to reach approximately 5 billion by CY2030 and approximately 15 billion by CY2047
- Corporate travel aided by Global Capability Centres: NASSCOM estimates 3,728 GCC units employing around 2.4 million professionals concentrated in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and NCR - the three cities posting the highest RevPAR growth in FY26
- Structural under-penetration of hotel rooms across Indian metros: Delhi NCR and Mumbai offer fewer than 1,400 hotel rooms per million population, materially below global peers, and Bengaluru has the lowest hotel-room density relative to its Grade-A office stock among 10 major Asian cities
- ICRA's March 2026 update expects pan-India premium hotel occupancy to hold at 72-74% through FY 2026-27, with RevPAR rising to Rs 6,200-6,500 in FY 2026-27, supported by demand events such as the ICC Men's T20 World Cup and the AI Impact Summit alongside continued lag in premium supply additions
- Supply continues to be constrained by high development costs, land scarcity and lengthy approvals, so demand is outpacing new inventory
- The rupee's 15% depreciation against the USD over three years has made domestic travel comparatively more cost-competitive than outbound trips and supports domestic industry pricing power
- Commercial Real Estate provides stable, high-margin annuity income that hedges the cyclicality of the hospitality segment, with an exit rental income run rate of Rs 280 million per month
- Pricing-led growth strategy in the hospitality portfolio, with the Average Daily Rate up 13% year-on-year to Rs 13,727
- Three leisure resorts totalling 446 keys (Rishikesh, NCR, Khandala) are in the initial phase of their lifecycle and yet to stabilise, and are expected to be an important driver of overall performance in coming years
- Globally, RevPAR growth is likely to moderate amid elevated geopolitical uncertainty, while performance increasingly hinges on asset quality, brand strength and location, and cost pressures, labour constraints and sustainability needs keep the focus on operational efficiency
- Inbound tourism is still normalising: India recorded approximately 90.2 lakh Foreign Tourist Arrivals in CY2025, a moderation over the prior year, with FTAs still below pre-pandemic peaks
- India is entering what management believes will be a defining decade for travel and hospitality, supported by rapid urbanisation, rising incomes, expanding aviation infrastructure, improving connectivity and increasing global engagement
- Total portfolio including pipeline has crossed the 5,000-key milestone
- Pipeline of approximately 1,655 rooms plus 0.9 msf of leasable area, comprising approximately 1,190 rooms and 0.9 msf under construction and approximately 464 rooms in planning
- Under construction: CIGNUS Powai Tower II (0.9 msf, Mumbai, Q4 FY27), Taj at Delhi International Airport (380 rooms, Q4 FY27), Athiva Resort & Spa at Varca, South Goa (205 rooms, FY28), Ritz Carlton at Hyderabad (330 rooms, Q4 FY29), Hyatt Regency at Airoli, Navi Mumbai (276 rooms, Q4 FY29)
- In planning: Premium Resort at Udaipur (approximately 144 rooms), Athiva Resort & Spa at Bambolim, North Goa (approximately 170 rooms), Athiva Resort & Convention Centre, Thiruvananthapuram (approximately 150 rooms)
- Commercial leasing: 2.4 msf leasable area with 2.1 msf leased as at March 2026, versus 1.6 msf leased at March 2025
- Residential: Phase 2 at Koramangala comprising 168 apartments under construction, plus a commercial unit of approximately 160,000 sq ft leasable area intended to be leased out

currentContext.expansion: Chalet is pursuing a high-conviction growth strategy of disciplined acquisitions of large-format hospitality assets and greenfield development of luxury and upper-upscale hotels in high-demand, under-penetrated micro-markets, with a stated plan to expand hotel inventory by around 50% (approximately 1,655 keys) and leasable area by over 37% from 2.4 msf to 3.3 msf in the next few years, taking total portfolio including pipeline past the 5,000-key milestone. Under construction are CIGNUS Powai Tower II (0.9 msf, Mumbai, completion expected Q4 FY27), the Taj at Delhi International Airport Terminal 3 (380 rooms, with 70 rooms targeted for commissioning by Q4 FY27 and the balance in the subsequent quarter; described elsewhere in the report as an approximately 385-390 room hotel being developed by subsidiary Chalet Airport Hotel Private Limited under a franchise agreement with The Indian Hotels Company Limited), Athiva Resort & Spa at Varca, South Goa (205 rooms, awaiting local approvals, expected completion FY 2027-28), the Ritz Carlton at Madhapur Mindspace, Hyderabad (330 rooms, to be received on warm shell basis from an SPV of Mindspace Business Parks REIT by Q4 FY28 with launch targeted Q4 FY29) and the Hyatt Regency at Airoli, Navi Mumbai (276 rooms, environmental clearance received and excavation started, launch targeted Q4 FY29) - together approximately 1,190 rooms and 0.9 msf. In planning are a premium resort at Udaipur (approximately 144 rooms, under design and approval, expansion potential being evaluated), Athiva Resort & Spa at Bambolim, North Goa (approximately 170 rooms, timelines estimated at around 36 months post approvals which follow closure of the acquisition) and Athiva Resort & Convention Centre at Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala (approximately 150 rooms) - approximately 464 rooms in total. During FY 2025-26 the Company added 129 additional rooms at Bengaluru Marriott Hotel Whitefield (8 suites added during the year, taking the total to 520 keys including 121 keys added in FY 2024-25), expanded the Khandala resort from 80 keys to 147 keys through the addition of 67 new rooms and a complete makeover, relaunching it as Athiva Resort & Spa, Khandala, and upgraded and rebranded the Faridabad resort as Aravali Marriott Resort & Spa, NCR with a pool bar, club house and refresh of rooms and public areas. The 152-key Four Points by Sheraton at Vashi is under renovation and is proposed to be rebranded under the Athiva brand. Three corporate development initiatives were signed during the year: a Binding Term Sheet to acquire Lakeview Mercantile Company Private Limited (potential approximately 170 room luxury resort at Bambolim, Goa; due diligence stage, closing expected during FY 2026-27), a Memorandum of Understanding for a warm-shell lease of a building at Madhapur, Hyderabad for a proposed approximately 330 room luxury hotel with approximately 36,255 sq ft of commercial/retail space, and a Binding Term Sheet to acquire Seasons Hotels Private Limited, which owns a resort at Udaipur, Rajasthan with around 150 rooms - completed in May 2026 after the year end, marking Chalet's entry into Rajasthan. In the rental and annuity space, nine towers of the Koramangala, Bengaluru residential project have been completed and handed over, with Phase 2 (two towers, 168 apartments) and a commercial building of approximately 160,000 sq ft under construction and expected to complete in FY 2026-27; Phase II of the Koramangala commercial development (0.2 msf) is under construction as part of the expansion of annuity office assets. Total keys of the Company and its subsidiaries stood at 3,389 as on March 31, 2026 across 11 hotels, with 2.4 msf of Grade A commercial real estate operational at 88% occupancy including area committed, plus 0.9 msf under development in Mumbai and 0.16 msf in Bengaluru. Management notes that in light of increasing complexities and high development costs it will increasingly evaluate brownfield opportunities, mixed-use developments and alternative structures to optimise capital efficiency.

risks.risk: Geopolitical shocks disrupting travel and energy markets
risks.note: The MD&A records that FY 2025-26 was marked by escalating trade tensions and tariff actions followed by the West Asia war, with disruptions around critical trade routes such as the Strait of Hormuz elevating input costs and disrupting trade flows and travel routes. Management states that a prolonged escalation could further weigh on global growth, and notes that beginning CY 2026 saw short-term impact from the West Asia war.

risks.risk: Aviation ecosystem disruption and passenger traffic volatility
risks.note: Hotel demand is highly correlated with aviation. The MD&A notes that Operation Sindoor and intermittent disruptions within the aviation ecosystem led to short-term uncertainty in travel sentiment and temporary volatility in passenger movement across select routes, and that March 2026 witnessed significantly lower air passenger traffic during the heightened turmoil, with complete normalcy potentially taking longer.

risks.risk: Discretionary spending sensitivity and moderating RevPAR growth
risks.note: The global hospitality outlook, while cautiously positive, remains challenged by continuing geopolitical uncertainties, elevated inflation and tighter financial conditions potentially impacting discretionary spending; management notes that amid elevated geopolitical uncertainty RevPAR growth is likely to moderate as pressure on travel sentiment and pricing power tempers performance.

risks.risk: Inflation, energy price volatility and tighter financial conditions
risks.note: The MD&A notes that inflation is anticipated to rise in CY 2026 before resuming its decline, driven largely by energy price volatility and supply-side disruptions, and that the RBI identified energy price volatility, geopolitical developments and climate-related disruptions as key upside risks to the inflation outlook. Growth is expected to be impacted by persistent supply-side risks, elevated energy prices and tighter financial conditions.

risks.risk: Uneven and still-normalising inbound tourism recovery
risks.note: Asia-Pacific international arrivals reached only approximately 91% of pre-pandemic levels in CY 2025, and India's Foreign Tourist Arrivals at approximately 90.2 lakh in CY2025 moderated over the prior year, remaining below pre-pandemic peaks and sensitive to global developments such as the West Asia conflict from March 2026.

risks.risk: Cost pressures, labour constraints and sustainability compliance needs
risks.note: Management states that over the next 3-5 years, while the industry moves into a structurally driven growth phase, cost pressures, labour constraints and sustainability needs will keep the focus on operational efficiency and differentiated experiences - a structural margin risk for an owned-asset hospitality operator.

risks.risk: Development and execution risk in a long-dated, approval-heavy pipeline
risks.note: The Board's Report describes multiple projects at different stages of completion (Airoli, Varca, Delhi Terminal 3, Madhapur Hyderabad, Kerala, Udaipur, CIGNUS Powai Tower 2), with the Bambolim resort dependent on approvals attained only post closure of the acquisition. The MD&A separately notes that supply is constrained by high development costs, land scarcity and lengthy approvals - the same conditions that create execution and timeline risk for Chalet's own pipeline.

risks.risk: Financing and leverage exposure across a capital-intensive build-out
risks.note: The Board's Report records that the Company avails credit facilities for capital expenditure, working capital and repayment of high-cost debt, and that during the year it availed additional borrowings and repaid existing debt, alongside outstanding debentures and commercial paper - leaving performance exposed to interest rates and refinancing conditions in a period the MD&A describes as one of tighter global financial conditions.

risks.risk: Concentration in a single hospitality-plus-real-estate business and limited geographic spread
risks.note: Per the BRSR, turnover is split only two ways - Accommodation and Food Service (62%) and Real Estate (38%) - across 11 hotels and one office in 5 states, with no international operations and no exports. Earnings therefore depend on a narrow set of Indian metro micro-markets.

risks.risk: Regulatory and structural approval dependency, including the pending amalgamation
risks.note: The Board's Report notes the Scheme of Arrangement and Amalgamation of Sonmil and Dukes with the Company has been filed and approval of the Hon'ble NCLT is awaited, leaving the intended corporate simplification and operational synergy contingent on a third-party approval.

one-line thesis: Chalet reported resilient full-year growth (Rev +18% ex-residential) but Q4FY26 faced a sharp 3% RevPAR decline driven by a 10-12% business disruption from West Asia tensions impacting Foreign Tourist Arrivals (FTA) and Mumbai-specific headwinds. The core investment thesis remains intact as management guides for a strong H2 recovery, supported by a INR 30bn capex pipeline largely funded by internal accruals and a high-margin CRE segment poised for a step-change in FY28.

growth verticals / optionality: 1) Leisure Diversification: Targeting 20% revenue from leisure via Udaipur, Khandala, Goa expansions. 2) CRE Upside: CIGNUS II commissioning in FY28 to drive step-change in rentals. 3) Cluster Strategy: Hyderabad expansion leveraging Mindspace ecosystem to dictate pricing. 4) Asset Sweating: F&B outlet expansions and rebranding (Four Points to Athiva, Courtyard to Marriott Aravali).

capital allocation: Deleveraging priority demonstrated (Net debt down INR 6bn in 2 years). Future growth to be funded by operating cash flows. Strategic minority dilution at DIAL project to manage balance sheet while retaining control. Dividend policy not explicitly detailed in snippet but implied secondary to growth funding.
risks & watch-items: 1) Geopolitical Tensions: Continued suppression of FTA and international MICE (10-12% business exposure). 2) Mumbai Concentration: High reliance on Mumbai market which faced unique headwinds (elections, construction noise at Powai). 3) Execution Risk: Delays in CIGNUS II or Hyderabad launch could defer cash flows. 4) Supply Glut: Potential increase in luxury supply in key micro-markets long-term.
management quality / tone: Confident in structural long-term story despite short-term 'unfortunate quarter'. Transparent about specific headwinds (West Asia, Mumbai elections). Emphasized discipline in capital allocation and strong balance sheet flexibility. Optimistic on H2 recovery and leisure demand substitution.
non-obvious takeaways: 1) The 'multiplier effect' loss: International executive cancellations dragged down associated domestic team travel, amplifying the FTA hit beyond direct foreign bookings. 2) Accounting nuance: INR 800cr Capex WIP is split across CWIP (INR 132cr), IPUC (INR 486cr), and Inventory (INR 269cr), obscuring the true scale of work-in-progress if looking only at the CWIP line item. 3) Hyderabad strategy: Taking a 'warm shell' on lease from sister concern Mindspace REIT significantly reduces upfront land risk and back-ends capex, improving ROCE profile.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Chalet is an owner, developer, asset manager and operator of high-end hospitality assets across key Indian metro markets, part of the K Raheja Corp Group, with 3,389 keys as on March 31, 2026.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Chalet owns, develops and asset-manages upscale and luxury hotels in India's principal business and travel destinations, operated largely through long-standing partnerships with global hospitality brands such as Marriott, Accor, Taj and Hyatt, and increasingly under its own ATHIVA brand launched in October 2025. The hotel portfolio is complemented by Grade A commercial office developments built on surplus FSI adjacent to the hotels, which supply stable annuity rental income, plus a single residential project at Koramangala, Bengaluru. Customers comprise brand owners, hotel guests, restaurant patrons, airline crews and tenants of the rented commercial spaces.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- ICRA expects Indian chain hotel demand to grow at a CAGR of 10.5% against supply CAGR of 9.1%, implying a sustained demand-supply gap
- Demand is underpinned by a broad mix of segments - business travel, leisure, MICE, weddings, pilgrimages and government/corporate delegations - supported by a growing economy, expanding travel infrastructure, new convention centres and wider airline connectivity
- Structural demographic shifts: urbanisation has risen from 28% (CY01) to an estimated 37% (CY24), still well below the US (84%), UK (85%) and China (67%); the middle class is projected to grow from 31% of population (FY21) to 61% by FY47
- Domestic tourism remains the dominant growth engine, with visitors projected to reach approximately 5 billion by CY2030 and approximately 15 billion by CY2047
- Corporate travel aided by Global Capability Centres: NASSCOM estimates 3,728 GCC units employing around 2.4 million professionals concentrated in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and NCR - the three cities posting the highest RevPAR growth in FY26
- Structural under-penetration of hotel rooms across Indian metros: Delhi NCR and Mumbai offer fewer than 1,400 hotel rooms per million population, materially below global peers, and Bengaluru has the lowest hotel-room density relative to its Grade-A office stock among 10 major Asian cities
- ICRA's March 2026 update expects pan-India premium hotel occupancy to hold at 72-74% through FY 2026-27, with RevPAR rising to Rs 6,200-6,500 in FY 2026-27, supported by demand events such as the ICC Men's T20 World Cup and the AI Impact Summit alongside continued lag in premium supply additions
- Supply continues to be constrained by high development costs, land scarcity and lengthy approvals, so demand is outpacing new inventory
- The rupee's 15% depreciation against the USD over three years has made domestic travel comparatively more cost-competitive than outbound trips and supports domestic industry pricing power
- Commercial Real Estate provides stable, high-margin annuity income that hedges the cyclicality of the hospitality segment, with an exit rental income run rate of Rs 280 million per month
- Pricing-led growth strategy in the hospitality portfolio, with the Average Daily Rate up 13% year-on-year to Rs 13,727
- Three leisure resorts totalling 446 keys (Rishikesh, NCR, Khandala) are in the initial phase of their lifecycle and yet to stabilise, and are expected to be an important driver of overall performance in coming years
- Globally, RevPAR growth is likely to moderate amid elevated geopolitical uncertainty, while performance increasingly hinges on asset quality, brand strength and location, and cost pressures, labour constraints and sustainability needs keep the focus on operational efficiency
- Inbound tourism is still normalising: India recorded approximately 90.2 lakh Foreign Tourist Arrivals in CY2025, a moderation over the prior year, with FTAs still below pre-pandemic peaks
- India is entering what management believes will be a defining decade for travel and hospitality, supported by rapid urbanisation, rising incomes, expanding aviation infrastructure, improving connectivity and increasing global engagement
- Total portfolio including pipeline has crossed the 5,000-key milestone
- Pipeline of approximately 1,655 rooms plus 0.9 msf of leasable area, comprising approximately 1,190 rooms and 0.9 msf under construction and approximately 464 rooms in planning
- Under construction: CIGNUS Powai Tower II (0.9 msf, Mumbai, Q4 FY27), Taj at Delhi International Airport (380 rooms, Q4 FY27), Athiva Resort & Spa at Varca, South Goa (205 rooms, FY28), Ritz Carlton at Hyderabad (330 rooms, Q4 FY29), Hyatt Regency at Airoli, Navi Mumbai (276 rooms, Q4 FY29)
- In planning: Premium Resort at Udaipur (approximately 144 rooms), Athiva Resort & Spa at Bambolim, North Goa (approximately 170 rooms), Athiva Resort & Convention Centre, Thiruvananthapuram (approximately 150 rooms)
- Commercial leasing: 2.4 msf leasable area with 2.1 msf leased as at March 2026, versus 1.6 msf leased at March 2025
- Residential: Phase 2 at Koramangala comprising 168 apartments under construction, plus a commercial unit of approximately 160,000 sq ft leasable area intended to be leased out

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Chalet is pursuing a high-conviction growth strategy of disciplined acquisitions of large-format hospitality assets and greenfield development of luxury and upper-upscale hotels in high-demand, under-penetrated micro-markets, with a stated plan to expand hotel inventory by around 50% (approximately 1,655 keys) and leasable area by over 37% from 2.4 msf to 3.3 msf in the next few years, taking total portfolio including pipeline past the 5,000-key milestone. Under construction are CIGNUS Powai Tower II (0.9 msf, Mumbai, completion expected Q4 FY27), the Taj at Delhi International Airport Terminal 3 (380 rooms, with 70 rooms targeted for commissioning by Q4 FY27 and the balance in the subsequent quarter; described elsewhere in the report as an approximately 385-390 room hotel being developed by subsidiary Chalet Airport Hotel Private Limited under a franchise agreement with The Indian Hotels Company Limited), Athiva Resort & Spa at Varca, South Goa (205 rooms, awaiting local approvals, expected completion FY 2027-28), the Ritz Carlton at Madhapur Mindspace, Hyderabad (330 rooms, to be received on warm shell basis from an SPV of Mindspace Business Parks REIT by Q4 FY28 with launch targeted Q4 FY29) and the Hyatt Regency at Airoli, Navi Mumbai (276 rooms, environmental clearance received and excavation started, launch targeted Q4 FY29) - together approximately 1,190 rooms and 0.9 msf. In planning are a premium resort at Udaipur (approximately 144 rooms, under design and approval, expansion potential being evaluated), Athiva Resort & Spa at Bambolim, North Goa (approximately 170 rooms, timelines estimated at around 36 months post approvals which follow closure of the acquisition) and Athiva Resort & Convention Centre at Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala (approximately 150 rooms) - approximately 464 rooms in total. During FY 2025-26 the Company added 129 additional rooms at Bengaluru Marriott Hotel Whitefield (8 suites added during the year, taking the total to 520 keys including 121 keys added in FY 2024-25), expanded the Khandala resort from 80 keys to 147 keys through the addition of 67 new rooms and a complete makeover, relaunching it as Athiva Resort & Spa, Khandala, and upgraded and rebranded the Faridabad resort as Aravali Marriott Resort & Spa, NCR with a pool bar, club house and refresh of rooms and public areas. The 152-key Four Points by Sheraton at Vashi is under renovation and is proposed to be rebranded under the Athiva brand. Three corporate development initiatives were signed during the year: a Binding Term Sheet to acquire Lakeview Mercantile Company Private Limited (potential approximately 170 room luxury resort at Bambolim, Goa; due diligence stage, closing expected during FY 2026-27), a Memorandum of Understanding for a warm-shell lease of a building at Madhapur, Hyderabad for a proposed approximately 330 room luxury hotel with approximately 36,255 sq ft of commercial/retail space, and a Binding Term Sheet to acquire Seasons Hotels Private Limited, which owns a resort at Udaipur, Rajasthan with around 150 rooms - completed in May 2026 after the year end, marking Chalet's entry into Rajasthan. In the rental and annuity space, nine towers of the Koramangala, Bengaluru residential project have been completed and handed over, with Phase 2 (two towers, 168 apartments) and a commercial building of approximately 160,000 sq ft under construction and expected to complete in FY 2026-27; Phase II of the Koramangala commercial development (0.2 msf) is under construction as part of the expansion of annuity office assets. Total keys of the Company and its subsidiaries stood at 3,389 as on March 31, 2026 across 11 hotels, with 2.4 msf of Grade A commercial real estate operational at 88% occupancy including area committed, plus 0.9 msf under development in Mumbai and 0.16 msf in Bengaluru. Management notes that in light of increasing complexities and high development costs it will increasingly evaluate brownfield opportunities, mixed-use developments and alternative structures to optimise capital efficiency.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Institutional asset-led ownership of large-format 'big box' hotels in gateway cities and locations within drivable distance of key airports, markets where supply is constrained by land scarcity, capex requirements and regulatory hurdles
- Long-standing partnerships with globally recognised hospitality brands including Marriott, Accor, Taj and Hyatt, giving access to global distribution and service standards
- Proprietary ATHIVA brand launched in October 2025, moving Chalet from pure asset owner to owner-operator, enabling capture of full operator margins and reduction of third-party management fees
- Mixed-use urban cluster model in which Grade A CIGNUS office assets adjacent to the hotels create a captive corporate base driving weekday occupancy and high-margin MICE demand, and enable shared infrastructure
- Commercial real estate annuity income hedges hospitality cyclicality, with 2.4 msf at 88% occupancy including area committed as of 31 March 2026
- Asset sweating through monetisation of surplus FSI at hotel sites and regular remodelling that adds revenue-generating F&B outlets such as Nox at The Westin Mumbai Powai Lake, El Bar at JW Marriott Mumbai Sahar and Souk at Novotel Pune Nagar Road
- Operating efficiency evidenced by a staff-to-room ratio of 0.99, against typical upper-upscale industry benchmarks of 1.1-2.1
- Strong sponsor with a real-estate development background (K Raheja Corp Group), aiding cost-effective project development and the ability to develop or lease mixed-use assets
- Experienced leadership at both Board and management level, with combined senior management experience of over 300 years
- Disciplined capital allocation with internal return thresholds on RoCE and payback that screen out smaller assets and remote locations

risks.body: 1) Geopolitical Tensions: Continued suppression of FTA and international MICE (10-12% business exposure). 2) Mumbai Concentration: High reliance on Mumbai market which faced unique headwinds (elections, construction noise at Powai). 3) Execution Risk: Delays in CIGNUS II or Hyderabad launch could defer cash flows. 4) Supply Glut: Potential increase in luxury supply in key micro-markets long-term.

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.
